title: Paradoxa, Emblemata, Aenigmata: Dionysius Andreas Freher (PH357)
shelf_note: Freher's emblem manuscript of Boehmist theosophy (BPH PH357); squarely within the library's Hermetic/theosophical scope.
structure_note: 88 pages, all OCR'd, 78 translated; the sampled leaves carry consecutive emblem numbers (58–60, 81–83, 135–136), so the order is plausible. Nothing broken.

other.note: Translation notes add interpretation that isn't on the page ("This describes the paradox of the mathematical and spiritual point", "This warns against interpreting spiritual origins in purely physical terms")

ocr_errors.ocr: Gläntze in der Sonnen Licht, wie du wilt, etc.
ocr_errors.image: Gläntze in der Sonnen Lufft [or Luſt], wie du wilt, etc.
ocr_errors.problem: the German motto's last noun is not 'Licht' (no dotted i, no c-h); it reads as Lufft/Luſt. The model swapped in the expected word

other.note: The image description says the centre of emblem 81 holds 'a radiant sun or monstrance-like object on an altar'. It actually shows a seated figure holding a branch, sitting on a block inside a ring of rays. The translation repeats this description.
<note> nested inside <note> in the translation (the image-description note contains an 'original:' note)

tr_errors.english: From the One <note>strange! and yet not strange</note> come things without number.
tr_errors.problem: the parenthesis that belongs to the motto was moved into a note

book_verdict: Clean. The emblem mottoes are transcribed and translated faithfully. The only slips are one misread German word on p.45 and a wrong description of an emblem's centre.

title: Actus et consecratio crismatis in cena domini
shelf_note: A decorated liturgical manuscript (Houghton fMS Typ 309: Maundy Thursday chrism rite, Canon of the Mass, Pater noster with chant). This is Catholic liturgy, outside the library's esoteric and early-science core, and no collection is given.
structure_note: Only 3 images for a whole manuscript, so this is a selection of leaves, not the codex. The record's title is just the first rubric. Pages 2–3 are the Te igitur and the Pater noster, not the chrism rite. A reader would take the record for the complete work.

tr_errors.problem: should be 'at the Lord's Supper' (Maundy Thursday)

other.note: The image description invents the miniature. The initial N is formed by two caryatid/mermaid figures with a fish/dragon on the diagonal; there is no bird. The OCR says 'a bird (likely a pelican) feeding its young', and the translation elaborates: 'depicts a pelican feeding her young from her own breast, a traditional symbol of self-sacrifice and Christ's sacrifice'. 'Pelican symbolism' is in the keywords.

tr_errors.source: omnibus orthodoxis atque catholice et apostolice fidei cultoribus
tr_errors.english: all those who hold to the true faith and the catholic and apostolic religion
tr_errors.problem: paraphrased ('all the orthodox and worshippers of the catholic and apostolic faith')

other.note: image description wrapped in <meta> in the translation pane

tr_errors.problem: over-literal for the doxology ('world without end')

book_verdict: The text is read and translated well. But page 1's image description invents a pelican in an initial that has none, and the translation builds a symbolic reading on it. The record is 3 selected leaves titled after the first rubric, and it sits on the edge of the library's scope.

title: M. Tullii Ciceronis Epistolae ad Atticum, ad M. Brutum, ad Quintum fratrem ... auctore Paulo Manutio Aldi filio
shelf_note: Aldine 1548 Cicero letters in the europeanlibraries collection: a classical source, appropriate to that collection.
structure_note: 701 pages, 697 with OCR, 695 translated, so near-complete. The OCR spelling convention flips between pages (u kept on p.176 and p.526, normalised to v on p.349: 'crevi', 'video'). This is O9, minor.

tr_errors.source: post a Pompeii procuratoribus sexcentis premi coeptus
tr_errors.english: Afterward, he began to be pressed by Pompey's agents.
to him, however, he is now paying
tr_errors.problem: the Pompey sentence is knotted: the 'cum ... tum' causal clause and the main clause run together

other.note: <meta>Catchword: et</meta>: 'et' is just the last word of the text line, not a catchword

tr_errors.source: pridie Nonas Februarias (image: prid. Non. Feb.)
tr_errors.problem: the day before the Nones of February is 4 February, not the 2nd. The letter's date is wrong.

tr_errors.source: de quibus ad te dolore, et lacrymis scribere prohibeor
tr_errors.english: about which I am prohibited from writing to you with grief and tears
tr_errors.problem: should be 'prevented BY grief and tears from writing'

ocr_errors.ocr: ut, quid possem prouidere, in mentem ueniret mihi, nisi quod praesens me ipse defenderem
ocr_errors.image: ut, quid possem prouidere, in menté non ueniret mihi, nisi q praesens me ipse defenderé
ocr_errors.problem: 'non' dropped. Cicero says nothing came to mind except defending himself in person; the transcription says something did. Sense reversed.

tr_errors.source: in mentem [non] ueniret mihi, nisi quod praesens me ipse defenderem
tr_errors.english: so that it came into my mind what I could provide, except that I should defend myself in person
tr_errors.problem: carries the dropped 'non' into English, so the sense is reversed

tr_errors.source: sed abesse hanc aetatem longe a sepulcro negant oportere
tr_errors.english: But they say that this age ought to be far from the grave
tr_errors.problem: 'negant' (they deny) is translated as 'they say', so the sentence says the opposite: a man of my age should NOT be far from his grave

tr_errors.source: etsi idem, te scribere, sperare melius
tr_errors.english: And yet [you say] the same, that you are writing to hope for better
tr_errors.problem: garbled: 'although he also said you wrote that you hope for better'

other.note: <header>LIB. XVI. EPIST.</header> repeated at the top of the translation pane

book_verdict: Good, fluent reading overall. But p.526 drops a 'non' in the OCR and renders 'negant' as 'they say', so two sentences on one page say the opposite of Cicero. P.349 also misdates a letter.

title: Horae beatae Mariae virginis (use of Paris)
shelf_note: An illuminated Book of Hours (Harvard), devotional and liturgical. It is outside the library's esoteric and early-science core, and no collection is given.
structure_note: 18 images of a full Book of Hours, i.e. the miniature pages only. Each image is a right-hand miniature page with a strip of the facing leaf's text at the left edge. The engine transcribed that strip as <margin> on every sampled page and the translator 'translated' the fragments.

ocr_errors.ocr: <margin>dicat. O / nobis qui / abrenunci / ente fan / ... cramen / tous.</margin>
ocr_errors.image: the cut-off line ends of the FACING leaf's text, visible at the left edge
ocr_errors.problem: a neighbour leaf's strip is read as this page's marginalia (about half the transcription)

tr_errors.source: Domine labia mea aperies et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam Deus
tr_errors.english: **D**omine labia mea <note>original: O Lord, open my lips</note> aperies et os me um annuntiabit lau dem tuam Deus
tr_errors.problem: the page's only real text is left in Latin. Half a line of English sits in a note labelled 'original', and the rest is untranslated.
word fragments from another leaf rendered as English

other.note: Broken markup in the translation: '<margin></margin>' then the content, then a stray '</margin>'

ocr_errors.ocr: <margin>ne patre nos / omnes atque / ... rtine. / gloria facer / ... mum.</margin>
ocr_errors.image: line ends of the facing leaf (a collect for St Catherine), cut off at the gutter
ocr_errors.problem: the neighbour leaf's strip is transcribed as marginalia on this page

tr_errors.problem: fragments are guessed into words that are not there: 'rtine' becomes the name 'Martin' (most likely '[Kathe]rine/[ma]rtine'); 'sacer' is misread as 'facer' and rendered 'to make'

other.note: Broken markup again: '<margin></margin>' followed by content and a stray '</margin>'

ocr_errors.image: Tout a par moy (the decorated initial is T)
ocr_errors.problem: the decorated initial is dropped, leaving the non-word 'Out'

ocr_errors.ocr: affu quon neme boye. Mesius retraict
ocr_errors.image: affin quon ne me voye. Me suis retraict
ocr_errors.problem: 'affin … voye' and 'Me suis' are misread, losing the sense ('so that no one sees me, I have withdrawn')

tr_errors.source: Tout a par moy affin quon ne me voye. Me suis retraict a vng lieu solitaire
tr_errors.english: Out of my own have I no one to whom I might complain. My mind withdraws to a solitary place.
tr_errors.problem: 'have I no one to whom I might complain' and 'My mind' are invented over the garbled OCR. The French says 'All alone, so that no one may see me, I have withdrawn to a solitary place.'
'se ravoie' means 'finds its way back', not 'is renewed'
a proper name invented from a fragment of the neighbour strip

book_verdict: On every sampled page the facing leaf's edge strip was transcribed and 'translated' as this page's marginalia. Page 5's real text was left untranslated. Page 14's French prayer is invented over a garbled read. Not showable.

title: Origenis opera omnia et quae eius nomine circumferuntur / Tomus primus.
shelf_note: De la Rue's 1743 Origen (De principiis, Contra Celsum): patristic Platonism, adjacent to the library's Hermetic and Platonist holdings.
structure_note: 541 pages, 522 OCR'd, 517 translated; the gap is probably plates/blanks. The OCR switches convention between pages: p.142 normalises long s, p.276 keeps ſ but misreads many as f ('Celfus', 'Jefu', 'fit' for 'ſit'), and p.407 normalises again. This is O9.

tr_errors.source: Vide l. 2. Origen. q. xj. num. 15.
tr_errors.problem: 'Origen.' here is Huet's Origeniana (rendered correctly elsewhere on the page)

ocr_errors.ocr: Celfus / Jefu / Theffalonicenfes / Moyfe / revelandus fit / fignis / falus
ocr_errors.image: Celſus / Jeſu / Theſſalonicenſes / Moyſe / revelandus ſit / ſignis / ſalus
ocr_errors.problem: long s systematically read as f, which breaks search for Celsus/Jesu/Moyses. The translation reads through it correctly.
the -n question particle is dropped (the translation still reads it as a question)

other.note: OCR contains a model-authored note: '<note>The following section contains scholarly apparatus and footnotes in sm[aller type]</note>'

book_verdict: Strong. Dense two-column Latin with footnotes is transcribed and translated faithfully, apparatus included. The flaws are cosmetic: long s read as f on one page, and the spelling convention changes from page to page.
